title: Algebraization of finite schemes over the thickenings of a scheme over a complete Noetherian ring
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $A$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]; put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $S_n=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^{n+1})$ for $n\ge0$. Let $X\to S$ be a separated morphism of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $X_n=X\times_SS_n$ [def-pc-base-change], with the closed immersions $X_n\to X_{n+1}$. Suppose given schemes $Y_n$ with finite morphisms $f_n:Y_n\to X_n$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and morphisms $Y_n\to Y_{n+1}$ making the squares with $X_n\to X_{n+1}$ commute and cartesian ($Y_n\cong Y_{n+1}\times_{X_{n+1}}X_n$ over $X_n$), and assume $Y_0\to S_0$ (the composite $Y_0\to X_0\to S_0$) is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Then there exist a finite morphism $f:Y\to X$ and isomorphisms $Y\times_XX_n\cong Y_n$ of $X_n$-schemes, compatible with the maps $Y_n\to Y_{n+1}$; moreover $Y$ is proper over $S$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09ZT (label lemma-algebraize-formal-scheme-finite-over-proper; there indexed by S_n = Spec(A/I^n), n >= 1), with its proof via Grothendieck's existence theorem (Theorem 088C, Remark reformulate-existence-theorem) and Lemma finite-pushforward-coherent

proof.text: (Setting.) Indices are shifted against Stacks: our $S_n,X_n,Y_n$ ($n\ge0$) are Stacks' $S_{n+1},X_{n+1},Y_{n+1}$. Let $j_n:X_n\to X$ and $i_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$ be the closed immersions (base changes of $S_n\to S$, $S_n\to S_{n+1}$), so $j_{n+1}\circ i_n=j_n$, and write $\mathcal G|_{X_n}=j_n^*\mathcal G$ for an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$, with the canonical isomorphisms $c_n:i_n^*(\mathcal G|_{X_{n+1}})\cong\mathcal G|_{X_n}$. Let $g_n:Y_n\to Y_{n+1}$ be the given maps, so $f_{n+1}\circ g_n=i_n\circ f_n$ and $(f_n,g_n):Y_n\to X_n\times_{X_{n+1}}Y_{n+1}$ is an isomorphism. $X_n\to S_n$ is separated and of finite type [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], and $S_n$ is Noetherian ($A/I^{n+1}$ is a quotient of a Noetherian ring); hence $X$ and every $X_n$ are locally Noetherian [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09ZT (lemma-algebraize-formal-scheme-finite-over-proper), proof; the shift of index as in the statement of the Lemma

proof.text: (The algebras $\mathcal A_n$.) Each $f_n$ is finite, in particular affine [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Put $\mathcal A_n=f_{n,*}\mathcal O_{Y_n}$: it is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-algebra [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](1), coherent as an $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-module because $f_n$ is finite and $X_n$ is locally Noetherian (step 1) [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-coherent], and $Y_n$ is, as an $X_n$-scheme, the relative spectrum of $\mathcal A_n$: $Y_n\cong\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_{X_n}(\mathcal A_n)$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](3).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09ZT (lemma-algebraize-formal-scheme-finite-over-proper), proof, first two sentences ('Set F_n = f_{n,*}O_{Y_n}. This is a coherent O_{X_n}-module as f_n is finite (Lemma 01Y6)')

proof.text: (The transition isomorphisms.) Since the square formed by $f_n,f_{n+1},i_n,g_n$ is cartesian and $f_{n+1}$ is affine, the base change map $\varphi_n:i_n^*\mathcal A_{n+1}=i_n^*f_{n+1,*}\mathcal O_{Y_{n+1}}\to f_{n,*}g_n^*\mathcal O_{Y_{n+1}}=f_{n,*}\mathcal O_{Y_n}=\mathcal A_n$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-algebras [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change](1),(2). So $(\mathcal A_n,\varphi_n)_{n\ge0}$ is a system of coherent modules with isomorphisms $i_n^*\mathcal A_{n+1}\cong\mathcal A_n$ as in [prop-weil-pbc-grothendieck-existence](b), and each $\varphi_n$ respects the algebra structures.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09ZT (lemma-algebraize-formal-scheme-finite-over-proper), proof, third sentence ('Using that the squares are cartesian we see that the pullback of F_{n+1} to X_n is F_n'), with Lemma 02KG (lemma-affine-base-change)

proof.text: (The support of $\mathcal A_0$ is proper over $S_0$.) $f_0$ is proper ([lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](c) applied with $h=\mathrm{id}_{X_0}$, which is proper), so $f_0(Y_0)$ is closed in $X_0$. If $x\notin f_0(Y_0)$, the open $V=X_0\setminus f_0(Y_0)$ has $f_0^{-1}(V)=\emptyset$, so $\mathcal A_0(V')=\mathcal O_{Y_0}(\emptyset)=0$ for every open $V'\subseteq V$ and the stalk $(\mathcal A_0)_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is $0$; thus $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal A_0)\subseteq f_0(Y_0)$. Now $Y_0\to S_0$ is proper by hypothesis, so the closed subset $Y_0$ of $Y_0$ is proper over $S_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties](1) (with its own scheme structure); $X_0\to S_0$ is separated and locally of finite type (step 1), so $f_0(Y_0)$ is a closed subset of $X_0$ proper over $S_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties](3). $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal A_0)$ is closed, $\mathcal A_0$ being quasi-coherent of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-module-support-proper-over-base](1), and contained in $f_0(Y_0)$, hence proper over $S_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties](2), [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09ZT (lemma-algebraize-formal-scheme-finite-over-proper), proof (the support condition of Remark 088F, left implicit there; written out with Lemmas 0CYL, 0CYN, 0CYQ(1) and Morphisms 056J)

proof.text: (Algebraizing the module.) By [prop-weil-pbc-grothendieck-existence](b) applied to $(\mathcal A_n,\varphi_n)$ (steps 2-4) there are a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ with support proper over $S$ and isomorphisms $\psi_n:\mathcal F|_{X_n}\to\mathcal A_n$ with $\varphi_n\circ i_n^*\psi_{n+1}=\psi_n\circ c_n$ for all $n$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09ZT (lemma-algebraize-formal-scheme-finite-over-proper), proof, fourth and fifth sentences (Grothendieck's existence theorem as reformulated in Remark 088F; the support of F is proper over S)

proof.text: (A closed subscheme carrying $\mathcal F$; supports of the auxiliary modules.) By [lem-weil-pbc-module-support-proper-over-base](2) there is a closed subscheme $Z\subseteq X$ with quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_Z$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] such that $Z\to S$ is proper and $\mathcal I_Z\mathcal F=0$. The modules $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal F=\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F$ and $(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal F)\otimes\mathcal F$ are quasi-coherent, with sections $\mathcal F(U)\otimes_R\mathcal F(U)$ (resp. the triple tensor product) over affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections]; these are finite $R$-modules since $\mathcal F(U)$ is [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](a), so the modules are of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](c), hence coherent on the locally Noetherian $X$ [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. $\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I_Z$ is a quasi-coherent quotient of $\mathcal O_X$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image], of finite type, hence coherent. All three are annihilated by $\mathcal I_Z$ (for local sections $a$ of $\mathcal I_Z$: $a(s\otimes t)=(as)\otimes t=0$ in the presheaf tensor product, hence in its sheafification; and $a\cdot\bar b=\overline{ab}=0$ in $\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I_Z$), so each has support proper over $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-support-proper-over-base](2) (the 'if' direction, with $Z$).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09ZT (lemma-algebraize-formal-scheme-finite-over-proper), proof ('As the completion functor is fully faithful (Theorem 088E)'): that the modules to which full faithfulness is applied have support proper over A is not written by Stacks; written out by the agent with Lemma 0CYS (2)<=>(3) and Lemma 0CYU (lemma-cat-module-support-proper-over-base)

proof.text: (Restricting tensor products.) For quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal G,\mathcal H$ the canonical map $\kappa:(\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal H)|_{X_n}\to\mathcal G|_{X_n}\otimes\mathcal H|_{X_n}$ (adjoint to $\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal H\to j_{n,*}(\mathcal G|_{X_n}\otimes\mathcal H|_{X_n})$, $s\otimes t\mapsto\eta(s)\otimes\eta(t)$, $\eta$ the unit of $j_n^*\dashv j_{n,*}$ [def-pc-module-pullback]) is an isomorphism: this is local, and over an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $X$ with $X_n\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}R/J$ ($J=I^{n+1}R$), $M=\mathcal G(U)$, $N=\mathcal H(U)$, the modules are $\widetilde M,\widetilde N$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], $\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal H|_U=(M\otimes_RN)^\sim$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections], the pullbacks are $(R/J\otimes_RM)^\sim$ etc. [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change], and $\kappa$ is the tilde of the canonical isomorphism $R/J\otimes_R(M\otimes_RN)\cong(R/J\otimes_RM)\otimes_{R/J}(R/J\otimes_RN)$ (both send $\bar r\otimes m\otimes n$ to $\bar r\otimes m\otimes n$, by the formulas on $\tau$ in those nodes). The $\kappa$ are natural in $\mathcal G,\mathcal H$ and compatible with the $c_n$ and with the associativity, symmetry and unit isomorphisms of $\otimes$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-symmetric-monoidal], since all of these are checked on the elements $\bar r\otimes m\otimes n$ over affine opens.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09ZT (lemma-algebraize-formal-scheme-finite-over-proper), proof ('the multiplication maps F_n (x) F_n -> F_n fit together'), which uses that the restriction of F (x) F to X_n is F_n (x) F_n; written out by the agent with Schemes Lemma 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback, literature/stacks-project/schemes.tex)

proof.text: (The multiplication.) Let $m_n:\mathcal A_n\otimes\mathcal A_n\to\mathcal A_n$ be the multiplication and $\mu_n=\psi_n^{-1}\circ m_n\circ(\psi_n\otimes\psi_n)\circ\kappa:(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal F)|_{X_n}\to\mathcal F|_{X_n}$ (step 7). Because $\varphi_n$ is an algebra map ($\varphi_n\circ i_n^*m_{n+1}=m_n\circ(\varphi_n\otimes\varphi_n)$ up to the isomorphism $i_n^*(\mathcal A_{n+1}\otimes\mathcal A_{n+1})\cong i_n^*\mathcal A_{n+1}\otimes i_n^*\mathcal A_{n+1}$, step 3), the $\psi_n$ are compatible with the $\varphi_n$ and $c_n$ (step 5), and $\kappa$ is compatible with the $c_n$ (step 7), we get $\mu_n\circ c_n=c_n\circ i_n^*\mu_{n+1}$. Both $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal F$ are coherent with support proper over $S$ (steps 5, 6), so by [prop-weil-pbc-grothendieck-existence](a) there is a unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\mu:\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ with $\mu|_{X_n}=\mu_n$ for all $n$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09ZT (lemma-algebraize-formal-scheme-finite-over-proper), proof, sixth sentence ('As the completion functor is fully faithful (Theorem 088E) we see that the multiplication maps F_n (x) F_n -> F_n fit together to give an algebra structure on F')

proof.text: (The unit.) $\mathcal O_X$ need not have support proper over $S$, so the unit is algebraized through $\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I_Z$ (step 6). Let $e_n:\mathcal O_{X_n}\to\mathcal F|_{X_n}$ be $\psi_n^{-1}$ composed with the unit $\mathcal O_{X_n}\to\mathcal A_n$. Multiplication by a local section $a$ of $\mathcal I_Z$ is zero on $\mathcal F$, so its pullback, multiplication by $j_n^\sharp(a)$, is zero on $\mathcal F|_{X_n}$; as $e_n(b)=b\,e_n(1)$, $e_n$ kills the image of $j_n^*\mathcal I_Z\to\mathcal O_{X_n}$ and, $j_n^*$ being right exact (a left adjoint [def-pc-module-pullback]), factors through $(\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I_Z)|_{X_n}=\mathcal O_{X_n}/\operatorname{im}(j_n^*\mathcal I_Z)$ as $\bar e_n$. The $\bar e_n$ are compatible with the $c_n$ since the $\varphi_n$ preserve units. As $\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I_Z$ and $\mathcal F$ are coherent with support proper over $S$ (step 6), [prop-weil-pbc-grothendieck-existence](a) gives a unique $\bar e:\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I_Z\to\mathcal F$ with $\bar e|_{X_n}=\bar e_n$; put $e:\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I_Z\xrightarrow{\bar e}\mathcal F$, so $e|_{X_n}=e_n$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09ZT (lemma-algebraize-formal-scheme-finite-over-proper), proof ('fit together to give an algebra structure on F'); the unit is not treated by Stacks and is written by the agent, using Lemma 0CYS (3)

proof.text: (The algebra axioms.) The two maps $\mu\circ(\mu\otimes1)$ and $\mu\circ(1\otimes\mu)\circ a$ from $(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal F)\otimes\mathcal F$ to $\mathcal F$ ($a$ the associativity isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-symmetric-monoidal]), the two maps $\mu$ and $\mu\circ c$ ($c$ the symmetry) from $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal F$, and the two maps $\mu\circ(e\otimes1)\circ l^{-1}$ and $\mathrm{id}$ from $\mathcal F$ to $\mathcal F$ ($l:\mathcal O_X\otimes\mathcal F\cong\mathcal F$ the unit isomorphism), are maps between coherent modules with support proper over $S$ (steps 5, 6). Their restrictions to each $X_n$ agree, since by steps 7-9 they are carried by $\psi_n$ and $\kappa$ to the corresponding maps for the commutative $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-algebra $\mathcal A_n$, which agree. By the injectivity in [prop-weil-pbc-grothendieck-existence](a) they agree. So $(\mathcal F,\mu,e)$ is a quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebra, and each $\psi_n:\mathcal F|_{X_n}\to\mathcal A_n$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-algebras (for the algebra structure on $\mathcal F|_{X_n}$ restricted through $\kappa$, given by $\mu_n$ and $e_n$).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09ZT (lemma-algebraize-formal-scheme-finite-over-proper), proof ('fit together to give an algebra structure on F'): the axioms, not written by Stacks, follow from the faithfulness part of Theorem 088E

proof.text: (The finite morphism $Y\to X$.) Let $\pi:Y=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_X(\mathcal F)\to X$ be the relative spectrum, an affine morphism with $\mathcal F\cong\pi_*\mathcal O_Y$ as $\mathcal O_X$-algebras and $\pi^{-1}(U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal F(U)$ for affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](2). $\mathcal F(U)$ is a finite $R$-module [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](a), so $R\to\mathcal F(U)$ is finite and $\pi$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09ZT (lemma-algebraize-formal-scheme-finite-over-proper), proof, last sentence ('Setting Y = Spec_X(F) finishes the proof')

proof.text: (Recovering the $Y_n$.) The base change $\pi_n:Y\times_XX_n\to X_n$ is finite, in particular affine [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a), and the base change map is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-algebras $\beta_n:j_n^*\pi_*\mathcal O_Y\to\pi_{n,*}\mathcal O_{Y\times_XX_n}$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change](1),(2). Composing, $\pi_{n,*}\mathcal O_{Y\times_XX_n}\cong\mathcal F|_{X_n}\xrightarrow{\psi_n}\mathcal A_n=f_{n,*}\mathcal O_{Y_n}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-algebras (step 10), so by the anti-equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](3) there is a unique isomorphism of $X_n$-schemes $\theta_n:Y\times_XX_n\to Y_n$ inducing it. Compatibility: $Y\times_XX_n=(Y\times_XX_{n+1})\times_{X_{n+1}}X_n$, and since $(f_n,g_n):Y_n\to X_n\times_{X_{n+1}}Y_{n+1}$ is an isomorphism, the equality $g_n\circ\theta_n=\theta_{n+1}\circ(\text{projection } Y\times_XX_n\to Y\times_XX_{n+1})$ is an equality of two $X_n$-morphisms $Y\times_XX_n\to X_n\times_{X_{n+1}}Y_{n+1}$ between schemes affine over $X_n$; by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](3) it suffices that they induce the same algebra map on pushforwards, which is the relation $\varphi_n\circ i_n^*\psi_{n+1}=\psi_n\circ c_n$ of step 5 together with the compatibility of base change maps with composition $j_n=j_{n+1}\circ i_n$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change](3). So $Y\times_XX_n\cong Y_n$ over $X_n$ (equivalently $Y\times_SS_n\cong Y_n$, as $X_n=X\times_SS_n$), compatibly with the maps $g_n$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09ZT (lemma-algebraize-formal-scheme-finite-over-proper), proof, last sentence ('Setting Y = Spec_X(F) finishes the proof'): the identification Y x_S S_n = Y_n is left to the reader by Stacks and written out here by the agent

proof.text: ($Y$ is proper over $S$.) Let $Z$ be as in step 6 ($Z\to S$ proper, $\mathcal I_Z\mathcal F=0$). The base change $Y\times_XZ\to Z$ is finite [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a), hence $Y\times_XZ\to Z\to S$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](c). The projection $Y\times_XZ\to Y$ is an isomorphism: over an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $X$ with $J=\mathcal I_Z(U)$, $Z\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}R/J$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] and $\pi^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal F(U)$ (step 11, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](2),(4)), so the projection over $U$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F(U)\otimes_RR/J=\mathcal F(U)/J\mathcal F(U)$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and $J\mathcal F(U)=0$ because $\mathcal I_Z\mathcal F=0$; these isomorphisms over the affine opens of $X$ glue. Hence $Y\to S$ is proper. (Equivalently: $\pi(Y)\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$, which is proper over $S$.)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09ZT (lemma-algebraize-formal-scheme-finite-over-proper), proof ('Moreover, Y is proper over S' in the statement; the proof only records that the support of F is proper over S): written out by the agent with Lemma 0CYS (3)
